skill.name: gen-env
skill.description: Creates, updates, or reviews a gen-env command for isolated local development instances with unique ports, hosts, Docker names, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Generate isolated localhost development environments for parallel project instances.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, localhost URLs, and expected local env file handling. Confirmed risk is limited to destructive Docker cleanup guidance and shell sourcing patterns that can cause local data loss or command execution if copied or tampered with.

remediation.issue: Broad Docker cleanup examples can remove multiple local development instances.
remediation.suggestion: Default to instance-specific cleanup, add a dry-run mode, and require explicit confirmation before removing containers, volumes, or networks.

remediation.issue: Sourcing .localnet.env treats the file as shell code.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a dotenv parser for generated key-value files, validate file ownership and format, and avoid sourcing files that can be edited by untrusted processes.

remediation.issue: Generated env examples include placeholder database URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Document that generated files must contain local-only values and should never include production credentials.

content.value_statement: Parallel local project copies can collide on ports, data, cookies, and Docker resources. This skill guides creation or review of a gen-env command that isolates each instance.
actual_capabilities: Defines instance identity from a workspace name for Docker, hosts, volumes, and containers.
Allocates unique localhost ports and stores reusable values in a lockfile.
Generates environment files with derived URLs for apps, APIs, databases, and tools.
Reviews existing gen-env scripts for naming, browser isolation, cleanup, and reuse behavior.
Adapts examples for Docker Compose, Tilt, direnv, CI jobs, and monorepos.
limitations: The skill provides implementation guidance, not a packaged executable command.
Project-specific service names, ports, and env files still need human review.
Generated cleanup commands can remove local Docker resources when used incorrectly.
It assumes localhost development workflows and may not fit remote environments.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Feature Branches
use_cases.description: Create separate local instances for multiple branches without port, cookie, or Docker volume conflicts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Dev Environments
use_cases.description: Add a consistent gen-env workflow that names resources, writes env files, and integrates with direnv or Docker Compose.

use_cases.title: Audit Local Isolation Scripts
use_cases.description: Review an existing script for safe naming, lockfile reuse, browser host separation, and scoped cleanup behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic gen-env Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small local app
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gen-env command for my project. It needs API, web, Postgres, and Redis ports, a workspace name, and a generated env file.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this gen-env script for port reuse, Docker Compose project naming, browser isolation, lockfile handling, and cleanup safety.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for Docker Compose and direnv
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt gen-env for Docker Compose and direnv. Include COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, service URLs, .envrc loading, and a safe clean command.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Environment Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gen-env strategy for a monorepo with shared tooling, Tilt integration, CI naming, many service ports, and isolated Docker resources.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for two local branches to run at the same time.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes a workspace name, isolated localhost hostnames, separate Docker project names, unique ports, and a reusable lockfile.

output_examples.input: A reviewer shares a script that only changes port numbers.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies missing instance identity, shared browser storage, incomplete Docker naming, and unsafe cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs CI-safe local environment generation.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends CI-specific names, random port allocation, forced regeneration, and cleanup scoped to the generated project name.

best_practices: Validate and sanitize workspace names before using them in hosts or resource names.
Use subdomain localhost hosts to isolate browser cookies and local storage.
Keep cleanup commands scoped to one generated project name whenever possible.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on different ports for browser isolation.
Do not run broad Docker cleanup commands without confirmation and a dry run.
Do not store real production credentials in generated local env files.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build or review a gen-env command for isolated local development instances.

faq.question: Does it install a ready-made tool?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and reference implementations that must be adapted to a project.

faq.question: Why use name.localhost instead of localhost?
faq.answer: Different localhost ports can still share browser cookies. Subdomains isolate browser state more reliably.

faq.question: Can it work with Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance uses COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, env files, and instance-specific resource names.

faq.question: Can generated env files contain secrets?
faq.answer: They should contain local-only values. Real credentials should stay in a proper secret manager.

faq.question: Is cleanup safe by default?
faq.answer: Cleanup should be scoped to one instance. Broad cleanup examples need confirmation and careful review.
